blocks.text: The module documentation defines action precedence, path and shell limitations, and the pure total decision contract. Imports and constants identify the catalog, risk bounds, and rule helpers used below.
blocks.title: Fail-closed policy contract

blocks.text: Request, Context, and Decision carry all policy inputs and outputs. Private verdict constructors make allow creation explicit before finalization rechecks its basis.
blocks.title: Requests, context, and verdicts

blocks.text: Verdicts are ranked, finalized against invalid settings and headless mode, and requests are type/range checked. Path decisions enforce secrets, protected paths, rules, plan mode, project containment, and defaults.
blocks.title: Validation and path verdicts

blocks.text: File tools normalize their paths and inspect glob patterns that could escape the project or reach sensitive locations. Multiple checks are combined with the worst verdict.
blocks.title: File-tool path analysis

blocks.text: Shell helpers identify sensitive glob matches, candidate paths, embedded scripts, executable options, dangerous environment variables, and denied program names in arguments.
blocks.title: Shell argument safety

blocks.anchor: def _redirect_verdicts(env: _Env, part: shellparse.Part, cwd: str | None) -> list[_V]:
blocks.text: Redirections are judged as reads or writes at their own risk. Each parsed command combines command rules with hidden-code, environment, argument, and redirect checks, and cd changes lexical cwd.
blocks.title: Shell parts and redirections

blocks.text: Leaving plan mode always asks unless denied by a rule. ask_user and tasks are matched as text-only interactions and otherwise follow interaction mode defaults.
blocks.title: Plan exit and interaction tools

blocks.anchor: def decide(request: Request | Mapping[str, Any], context: Context) -> Decision:
blocks.text: decide catches every exception and returns a safe denial. _decide validates context, risk, tool, paths, and merged rules before dispatching to shell, plan-exit, interaction, or file-tool logic.
blocks.title: Public decision boundary

gotchas: The policy cannot see code fetched or executed indirectly by an allowed program.
Symlink containment is left to executors.
tainted is accepted but has no effect in this patch.
how_it_works: Validates request vocabulary, arguments, roots, and risk
Evaluates hard denies, rules, plan mode, path scope, and mode defaults
Analyzes shell parts, arguments, redirections, hidden code, and environment hazards
Combines multi-part verdicts by deny > ask > allow
outputs: Decision with action, reason, matched rule, effective risk, and allow basis
purpose: This module validates tool requests, merges trusted policy layers, checks paths and shell syntax, and returns a safe Decision. It never performs I/O or raises through its public entry point; malformed input and internal failures become denials.
summary: Pure, fail-closed policy engine for deciding whether a client tool call is allowed, asks, or denied.
